feedback: Based only on iteration 0 (entityR2A and its outcome table). The baseline ended off_track on all 60 trials, with progress 0.11 to 0.16, max_error about 0.06 at the off-track floor, 1 to 2 line-loss events per run, and steering_oscillation 0.14 to 0.17. So the robot drifts off the tape rather than oscillating. The Integrator has widened the controller's correction (kp 4 to 6, kd 0.3 to 0.6) to work with your ±0.04 m span, so the controller is not the limit you need to fix on this geometry. Do not read the result of this candidate into this feedback. Decide the next change from what the race shows. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more and max_error stays at the 0.06 m limit, the sensor footprint does not cover the tape far enough out, so widen the span further (for example ±0.06 at 0.03 m spacing, within the ±0.08 limit). If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25, the sensor lead is the suspect, so reduce sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03. If rms_error is high while line_loss_events are zero, the footprint is too large for the 25 mm tape, so try sensor_size 0.008. body_width cannot help: the off-track limit cannot rise above about 0.0575 within the allowed range, so do not spend a change on body_width.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events remain at 1 or more and max_error stays near 0.06 m in the next race, widen sensor_positions to x = ±0.06 with five sensors at 0.03 m spacing. Evidence: iteration 0 had 1 to 2 line-loss events per run with max_error 0.0603 to 0.0656, so the current span of ±0.03 (now ±0.04) is not covering the drift.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 after the gain increase, move every sensor's y from 0.05 to 0.03, keeping the other geometry fixed. Evidence: iteration 0 steering_oscillation was 0.14 to 0.17, so there is headroom, but a higher gain at a long sensor lead could push it up.

If rms_error is above about 0.03 with zero line-loss events, try sensor_size 0.008 to tighten the footprint on the 25 mm tape. Evidence: iteration 0 rms_error was 0.0256 to 0.0297 with 1 to 2 line-loss events, so this is only a secondary lever for now.
